locus.section: Beobachtung der totalen Mondfinsterniss 1852 Januar 6 auf der Breslauer Sternwarte.

Die nahe Uebereinstimmung der Beobachter in den meisten Momenten zeigt, dass beide die Grenze des Schattens in ziemlich gleichmässiger Weise auffassten. Ich beobachtete in der Kuppel an dem 4½f. Fraunhofer, Herr Günther in einem Fenster des Thurms an dem 4füss. Fraunhofer. Die Farbe des verdunkelten Mondes war in der gewöhnlichen Weise röthlich oder lichtbraun, mehr grau in der Nähe der Schattengrenze. Mit der heraufkommenden Dämmerung wurde der verdunkelte Mond immer undeutlicher, namentlich im Fernrohr; aber auch für das blosse Auge war derselbe in einiger Entfernung vom Horizonte nicht mehr zu erkennen, obgleich der Dünste nicht allzuviele waren und die Aussicht hier eine der freiesten ist, welche man wünschen kann. Das Hervortreten des ersten Sonnenrandes am Horizonte beobachtete ich um 20h 0′ 15″ mittl. Zt., gegen 2½′ früher, als eine genaue Rechnung des Sonnenaufgangs ergiebt. Mit Anbringung einer Depression des Horizontes von 10′5 (wegen etwa 100 Fuss Erhöhung über der Ebene) vermindert sich diese Abweichung bis auf etwa 1 Zeitminute. Das Thermometer zeigte +1°4 R., das Barometer 334,30 P. L. bei mässigem Südwinde.
Die obigen Zeitangaben sind mittl. Zeit. Die Zeitbestimmungen sind am Abend vorher und nachher von Herrn Günther an dem (alten Bessel’schen) Passage-Instrument gemacht.
Breslau 1852, Janr. 9.
J. G. Galle.

text.en:
The total lunar eclipse of 6 January was observed here, for as long as the Moon was above the horizon and visible, in the following manner:
 | Galle. | Günther.
Beginning of the eclipse | 17h 29′ 37″ | 17h 29′ 19″
Grimaldi, centre | 17 34 21 | 17 33 54
Aristarchus, centre | 17 38 26 | 17 38 24
Kepler, centre | 17 41 5 | 17 41 2
Copernicus, I. limb | 17 48 44 | 17 48 5
— centre | 17 50 9 | 
— II. limb | 17 51 4 | 17 50 0
Plato, centre | 17 54 58 | 17 54 36
Tycho, I. limb | 18 4 1 | 18 4 3
— centre | 18 4 51 | 
— II. limb | 18 5 46 | 18 5 10
Plinius (?), bright spot | 18 7 21 | 
(?) |  | 18 10 59
Beginning of totality | 18 29 57 | 18 29 27
The close agreement of the observers at most moments shows that both perceived the edge of the shadow in a fairly uniform way. I observed in the dome with the 4½-foot Fraunhofer, Mr Günther in a window of the tower with the 4-foot Fraunhofer. The colour of the darkened Moon was, as usual, reddish or light brown, more grey near the edge of the shadow. As dawn came on, the darkened Moon grew ever less distinct, especially in the telescope; but even to the naked eye it could no longer be made out at some distance from the horizon, although the haze was not excessive and the view here is one of the clearest one could wish for. I observed the appearance of the Sun's first edge at the horizon at 20h 0′ 15″ mean time, about 2½′ earlier than an exact calculation of sunrise gives. Allowing for a horizon depression of 10′5 (on account of about 100 feet of elevation above the plain), this discrepancy is reduced to about 1 minute of time. The thermometer showed +1°4 Réaumur, the barometer 334.30 Paris lines, with a moderate south wind.
The times given above are mean time. The time determinations were made by Mr Günther on the evening before and after, at the (old Bessel) transit instrument.
Breslau, 9 January 1852.
J. G. Galle.

Den Austritt zu sehen verhinderten der tiefe Stand und die helle Dämmerung. Der Kernschatten war diesmal ungewöhnlich gut begrenzt. During totality I measured with the heliometer the diameter of the Moon at the position angles 0° and 90°. At this time the Moon appeared so faintly illuminated, on account of its low altitude behind the haze of the horizon and the dawn that had already set in, that I could use only the weakest magnification. With this, however, the north and south limbs could be seen quite distinctly, and from the mean of 5 measurements I obtained, at 14h 21′5 Königsberg sidereal time, the radius of the Moon for the position angle = 0°, (corrected for refraction) = 15′ 47″8. Reduced to the center of the earth, this gives 15′ 55″1. According to the Nautical Almanac the latter radius at the same time is = 15′ 56″2, so the observed one is 1″1 smaller. The measurements of the radius perpendicular to this were much less precise, because the eastern limb of the Moon appeared so faint that it could be made out only with difficulty. From the mean of 6 measurements I obtained, for the position angle = 90°, the apparent radius of the Moon freed from refraction, at 13h 59′6 Königsberg sidereal time = 15′ 57″1, from which follows the radius seen at the same time from the center of the earth = 15′ 56″1, 0″8 greater than according to the Nautical Almanac.
Königsberg, 1852, Jan. 20.
C. A. F. Peters.
